name: Añelo
shape: geoBoundaries, the department it is named for

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo and Dolcetto fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
